headline.purpose: Modal headers, major section heads within a view.

components.name: Note Card
components.description: Container for a saved research note. Two-column grid: reorder strip + content. Flat at rest.
components.html:
The annotated margin as design doctrineSelection note · Jun 7, 14:23

Every mark on the page must earn its place. Decoration is the absence of thought.

narrative.overview:
Øde is the layer of precision that sits alongside original research. Every element in this system asks: is this the mark of someone who read carefully, or someone who decorated a template? The answer is always the former. Surfaces are spare. Type does the structural work. The ochre accent appears like a pencil underlining — rare, intentional, exact.

The palette is built around the principle that warmth belongs to the accent, not the background. Crisp white pages carry the content; deep ochre (the pigment-name hue, not a tech-brand orange) marks what matters. The neutral ramp leans cool — a slate family with faint blue undertones — so the ochre reads as a considered mark against an academic field, not a product accent against a warm-neutral SaaS canvas.

This system explicitly rejects: the white-bubble-on-dark-sidebar AI chat aesthetic (ChatGPT, Perplexity), the warm-cream-with-rounded-everything SaaS register (Notion-adjacent products), and the 'browser extension grey' starting point — the current state before this system was established.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces at rest; tonal separation between surface and white creates depth without shadows
Single accent color used at ≤10% surface area: ochre for primary actions and active states
Inter alone, tuned through weight and size — five tracked roles, no display/body split
8px radius throughout; gently curved but not soft
Transitions at 120–160ms ease-out; state changes only, no choreography

rules.name: The One Ochre Rule
rules.body: Ochre appears once per screen in a meaningful way: the primary action, or the active selection state. Never both on the same screen at full saturation.

rules.name: The No-Tinted-Background Rule
rules.body: Surface exists; it is the only background that carries any hue. Body backgrounds, modal overlays, and panel containers do not use cream, beige, warm white, or cool blue.

rules.name: The Single Family Rule
rules.body: Inter is the only typeface. Adding a display face, a serif for headings, or a mono for labels is forbidden.

rules.name: The Weight Rule
rules.body: Labels are 700; body is 400. Never use 600 as the sole differentiator between a label and body text at the same size.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, note items, messages, and folder chips have no ambient shadow at rest. Introducing a hover shadow on note cards or chat messages is prohibited.

rules.name: The Modal-Last Rule
rules.body: Modals are used only for irreversible multi-step confirmations. Single-step confirmations and folder/project creation use inline forms.

dos: Do use ochre exclusively for the single most important interactive signal on any given screen
Do keep white as the card background in every view — notes, messages, modals, inputs are always white
Do use tonal separation (surface panel + white card) as the primary depth affordance
Do use focus-visible focus rings (2px solid ochre, 2px offset) on every interactive element
Do put white text on any ochre fill
Do keep transitions at 120–160ms ease-out, state changes only
Do use danger red for destructive actions with white text
donts: Don't use a left-border stripe (border-left > 1px with a brand color) as a state indicator
Don't introduce a cream, sand, parchment, or warm-neutral body background
Don't use the dark-sidebar / white-bubble chat layout — this is the ChatGPT/Perplexity anti-reference
Don't add ambient hover shadows to note cards, message bubbles, or list items
Don't use ochre as body text on a white background — contrast is only ≈3.7:1
Don't render ghost/secondary buttons with transparent borders on a white card background
Don't use generic button copy: 'OK', 'Yes', 'Cancel'. Always verb + object
